task.description:
Implement PAR-05, PAR-06, PIN-02 in FULL per their validated Step 01 design artefacts. Implement PIN-01 SCOPED ONLY to AC3 (variable_schema validation, resolves against the real existing variable_schemas table), AC4 (pin_overrides application), and AC5 (deterministic ordering of whatever pins are actually produced). PIN-01 AC1 (catalog-version resolution) and AC2 (module-ref resolution) are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this batch -- tracked separately as ISS-0672 / GH-306 (AC1: service_catalog has no version/status column; AC2: PLC-01 module catalog does not exist yet). Do NOT attempt AC1/AC2. Per Step 01b validator routing: implement the catalog_entry/module resolution branches only as far as the design doc's explicitly-marked-provisional stopgap queries (see each design's Public Interface section), and for any reference that does not resolve under that degenerate/stopgap reading, return the design's documented error taxonomy values UnresolvedCatalogRef / UnresolvedModuleRef -- never a silent no-op, never a TODO, never a stub that fabricates success. PAR-06 also requires running its Type C migration YAML (templates/specs/par06-instance-projections-event-window.migration.yaml) via the codegen migration tooling to produce the actual .sql migration file, then applying it. PIN-02 touches src/engine/instance.zig at the event-append call site for INSTANCE_STARTED -- implement exactly per the pin-02-pin-set-in-instance-started.md design (pin set recorded durably in the INSTANCE_STARTED event payload). Read .env directly for BPM_DB_URL / BPM_TEST_DB_URL -- do not hardcode ports anywhere; this host remaps db/db_test to non-default ports via a local docker-compose.override.yml.

REWORK 1 (triggered by SECURITY-REVIEWER Step 2c FAIL, handoff bfd75fb4-1567-4757-8e49-be5cda7d1ed4):
- [BLOCKER] INV-1 FAIL: src/engine/pin_resolver.zig:197 (resolveServiceCatalogRef(), called unconditionally from PinResolver.resolve() at every SERVICE_TASK node, reached from src/engine/instance.zig InstanceStore.create() Step d.5 on the LIVE POST /api/v1/instances path) filters service_catalog by "owner_tenant_id = bpm_effective_tenant_id()". bpm_effective_tenant_id() is a SQL function that migrations/028_adp02_tenant_scope_persistence.sql defined for the retired LEGACY_RLS model and that migrations/GBL-116_tnt07_rls_cleanup.sql, GBL-123_rls_removal.sql, GBL-130_iss503_guard_tenant_type_scope.sql, and GBL-131_iss0100_guard_tc_slug_scope.sql all DROP FUNCTION -- these are real, applied migrations. In a fully-migrated environment the function does not exist: every instance-start with a resolvable SERVICE_TASK service_id fails with Postgres 42883 (untyped HTTP 500). Even if resurrected, src/db/pool.zig only sets the bpm.tenant_id session variable in LEGACY_RLS mode (pool.zig:277-282) -- SCHEMA mode (the current target architecture) never sets it -- so the predicate could not correctly tenant-scope even then.
  FIX REQUIRED: Add a tenant_id field to PinResolver.ResolutionInput (pin_resolver.zig:58-63), thread it from instance.zig's existing request-tenant context into PinResolver.resolve(), and have resolveServiceCatalogRef() bind it as a parameterized ::uuid against service_catalog.owner_tenant_id -- mirror src/repository/service_catalog.zig's getServiceForTenant() (service_catalog.zig:266-292), which already implements this correctly and is the pattern the design doc (src/design/pin-01-dependency-version-resolution.md:269-272) claimed to reuse but did not. Remove the bpm_effective_tenant_id() reference entirely; do not attempt to resurrect the dropped SQL function.
- Re-submit for SECURITY-REVIEWER Step 2c re-review after this fix. PAR-05 and PAR-06 do NOT need rework -- SECURITY-REVIEWER PASSed both as implemented. Only pin_resolver.zig's resolveServiceCatalogRef() tenant-scoping is blocking.


REWORK 2 (triggered by TEST-DESIGNER Step 3, handoff 67a40957-17d3-41d0-b28c-f9edd4870c4d):
TEST-DESIGNER wrote real integration tests against real PostgreSQL for PAR-05 (full scope),
PAR-06 (full scope), and PIN-01 AC3/AC4/AC5 (in-scope portion), and those tests exposed 3
BLOCKER-severity correctness defects in this run's OWN Step 2a implementation -- these are
this run's own code failing this run's own new tests against this run's own MUST acceptance
criteria, so per ORCHESTRATOR.md Section on WF-03 trigger recognition ("if the failure is
that step's own acceptance criteria... it is rework within the active run") this is routed
back to you as rework, not deferred to a separate WF-03 run. Fix all three:

- [BLOCKER] ISS-0676 / GH-718 (PAR-05): src/db/partition_conversion.zig
  PartitionConverter.createParent() issues "CREATE TABLE events_part (LIKE events INCLUDING
  DEFAULTS INCLUDING IDENTITY) PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)". LIKE ... INCLUDING DEFAULTS
  INCLUDING IDENTITY does NOT copy constraints (confirmed live against PostgreSQL 15.14) --
  events_part ends up with zero constraints. backfillOneMonth() (AC1/AC3) and swap() (AC4)
  both issue "INSERT INTO events_part ... ON CONFLICT (event_id, created_at) DO NOTHING"
  which fails with 42P10 ("no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT
  specification") on the first insert, because no such constraint exists on events_part.
  FIX: add INCLUDING CONSTRAINTS (and likely INCLUDING INDEXES) to the LIKE clause in
  createParent(), OR explicitly issue ALTER TABLE events_part ADD PRIMARY KEY (event_id,
  created_at) immediately after CREATE TABLE -- matching how 1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql
  declares this PK explicitly in its own from-scratch path. Verify live against real Postgres,
  not just by reading the DDL.

- [BLOCKER] ISS-0677 / GH-719 (PAR-06 AC4): PAR-06 AC4 requires instances.last_event_at
  (and first_event_at) to be advanced in the SAME transaction as every event append.
  src/event_store/store.zig Store.append() implements this correctly (Step 5 UPDATE,
  COALESCE on first_event_at). BUT src/engine/instance.zig InstanceStore.create() -- the
  call site that writes every instance''s first event, INSTANCE_STARTED -- does NOT go
  through Store.append(); it issues its own hand-rolled INSERT INTO events statement that
  never touches the window columns. There are 12 separate raw INSERT INTO events call sites
  in instance.zig (create(), completeTask(), cancel(), setError(), others); none maintain
  the PAR-06 window columns, so every instance starts with first_event_at/last_event_at NULL.
  FIX: route instance.zig''s event-append call sites through Store.append() instead of raw
  INSERT (preferred -- also closes the sibling ES-05 validation gap PIN-02''s own design doc
  flagged), or widen each hand-rolled INSERT site to also perform the window-maintenance
  UPDATE that Store.append() Step 5 performs. Audit ALL 12 call sites, not just create().

- [BLOCKER] ISS-0679 / GH-721 (PIN-01 AC3): src/engine/pin_resolver.zig
  PinResolver.validateVariableSchema() calls registry.validatePayloadAgainstSchema(allocator,
  schema_text, value_json) passing a SINGLE FIELD VALUE (e.g. the scalar 5 for a variable
  named count) as value_json. validatePayloadAgainstSchema()''s contract requires payload to
  be a JSON OBJECT (isJsonObject() guard checks the input starts with "{"). A bare scalar
  never satisfies this, so every conforming scalar-valued variable is incorrectly rejected as
  a VariableSchemaViolation -- AC3''s accepting half can never pass. FIX: wrap the field value
  in a synthetic one-key object and the field''s schema in a synthetic one-property object
  schema before calling validatePayloadAgainstSchema(), OR add a lower-level entry point in
  registry.zig / src/tools/json_schema.zig that validates a single JSON value against a single
  schema document directly (no isJsonObject guard) and call that instead.

Do NOT touch PIN-02 (5/5 new tests already pass) or PIN-01 AC5 (2/2 pass) -- both are
correctly implemented already, per TEST-DESIGNER''s report. ISS-0678/GH-720 (a bug in the
pre-existing PAR-06 migration test file itself, not in this batch''s production code) and
ISS-0680/GH-722 (a PinResolver.resolve() memory leak on error paths, MAJOR but not an AC
correctness failure) are correctly filed-and-forwarded to the global queue for their own
later WF-03 runs -- do NOT fix those here, they are out of scope for this rework.

After fixing, re-run the specific new test targets TEST-DESIGNER wired (see build.zig:
test-integration-par05, test-integration-par06-reconstruction, and the PIN-01 AC3/AC4 cases
in pin01_test_root.zig / tests/integration/pin01_ac345_resolution_test.zig) against real
Postgres (BPM_TEST_DB_URL from .env) and report the exact pass/fail counts. Do not claim a
fix without a real green run.


REWORK 3 (FINAL rework budget -- max_rework=3; triggered by ORCH review of REWORK 2's own
result, not a new gate FAIL): REWORK 2 correctly fixed ISS-0676/0677/0679 and correctly
identified ISS-0682 as an out-of-scope test-fixture bug (wrong-case literal in a hand-crafted
fixture, not production code). But ISS-0681/GH-724 is NOT the same class as ISS-0682: it is a
genuine gap in this run's OWN PAR-05 production code, discovered by this run's OWN new PAR-05
test (TC-PAR-05-06) failing against this run's OWN MUST AC5 ("a mismatch raises
ConversionRowCountMismatch and the inverse rename restores the original events"). Per the same
"own acceptance criteria = in-run rework, not deferral" rule that routed ISS-0676/0677/0679
back to you, this is rework, not a queue item -- fix it now while rework budget remains
(this is rework 3 of 3, the last one; if it cannot be fully resolved, say so honestly and
report PARTIAL/FAIL, do not fabricate a PASS):

- [BLOCKER] ISS-0681 / GH-724 (PAR-05 AC5): PartitionConverter.backfillOneMonth()
  (src/db/partition_conversion.zig) calls partition_attach.zig's attachPartitionTimed()
  directly for each month partition but never inserts/upserts a row into
  plat_partition_catalog afterward -- that bookkeeping only happens in
  src/scheduler/partition_maintenance.zig's ensurePartitionAttached() (PAR-02's daily job),
  which PartitionConverter never calls. reconcileOrRollback() (Step 6, AC5) discovers which
  partition pairs to compare via a self-join on plat_partition_catalog filtered by
  parent_table = events_legacy / parent_table = events; with zero rows for any
  events_part-derived partition, the join is always empty, the mismatch-detection loop body
  never runs, and the function returns success unconditionally -- so AC5's core guarantee
  (a real row-count divergence is detected and rolled back) currently never fires. Confirmed
  live: TC-PAR-05-06 (deliberately corrupts a post-swap partition's row count, expects
  ConversionRowCountMismatch) fails with "expected error.ConversionRowCountMismatch, found
  void".
  FIX: have backfillOneMonth() insert/upsert its own plat_partition_catalog row
  (table_name=partition_name, parent_table='events_part', state='ATTACHED') immediately
  after each successful attachPartitionTimed() call -- mirror ensurePartitionAttached()'s own
  INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (table_name) DO UPDATE shape (factor it into a small shared helper
  both partition_maintenance.zig and partition_conversion.zig call, if that is the cleaner
  fix). ALSO: swap()'s rename from events_part to events (and events to events_legacy) needs
  the corresponding plat_partition_catalog.parent_table values updated at rename time, or the
  AC5 self-join predicate will still never match real rows even after the population gap is
  fixed -- ISS-0681's own filed prevention notes flag this as a second half of the same fix.
  Verify TC-PAR-05-06 passes live against real Postgres after the fix, not just by code
  reading.

Do NOT touch ISS-0682/GH-725 (confirmed genuine test-fixture bug, correctly out of scope,
stays queued for its own run) or ISS-0678/GH-720 or ISS-0680/GH-722 (both already
out-of-scope per rework 2's instructions, unchanged).

This is the last rework cycle available (rework_count will be 3/3 after this). If
ISS-0681's fix cannot be completed and verified green in this pass, report PARTIAL (not
PASS) with the specific remaining gap named, and ORCH will escalate per
docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md's rework policy rather than accept an
unverified claim.
acceptance_criteria: PAR-05: online partition conversion implemented per design, zig build exits 0
PAR-06: time-bounded reconstruction implemented per design; migration YAML materialized to SQL via codegen tooling and applied to BPM_DB_URL and BPM_TEST_DB_URL

PIN-01: AC3 (variable_schema validation), AC4 (pin_overrides), AC5 (deterministic ordering) implemented; AC1/AC2 explicitly NOT attempted; unresolved catalog/module refs return UnresolvedCatalogRef/UnresolvedModuleRef per design error taxonomy, not a silent no-op or TODO
PIN-02: pin set durably recorded in INSTANCE_STARTED event payload at the src/engine/instance.zig call site, per design
zig build exits 0 with no new warnings
zig build test exits 0 for any unit-level tests colocated with the implementation (integration tests are TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-RUNNER scope, Steps 3-4)
No implementation deviates from the validated Step 01 design artefacts without a documented, justified reason

Any NEW incidental defect found while implementing (not PIN-01 AC1/AC2, already tracked) is filed as its own ISS + GitHub issue and forwarded to the global queue per core-directives.md -- not fixed inline unless it genuinely blocks this step

result.summary: REWORK 3/3 (FINAL): fixed ISS-0681/GH-724 (PAR-05 AC5). backfillOneMonth() now upserts a plat_partition_catalog row (table_name=partition_name, parent_table=events_part, state=ATTACHED) immediately after each successful attachPartitionTimed() call, via a new shared helper partition_maintenance.upsertPartitionCatalogRow() (factored out of ensurePartitionAttached()'s own INSERT...ON CONFLICT shape so PAR-02's daily job and PAR-05's conversion share one definition). swap() now updates plat_partition_catalog.parent_table at rename time in the same transaction (events -> events_legacy, events_part -> events). While verifying live, found reconcileOrRollback() itself had a second, deeper defect beyond the population gap: its self-join required plat_partition_catalog rows for BOTH parent_table=events AND parent_table=events_legacy, but events_legacy (the pre-PAR-01 unpartitioned source table after rename) is never itself split into catalog-registered monthly children -- per AC5's own text ("per-month count(*) is compared between events_legacy and the new partitions") and the design doc's own Open questions section 5, which flags this exact gap. This made the self-join structurally unmatchable regardless of the population fix, so it genuinely blocked completing ISS-0681 and was fixed as part of the same rework: reconcileOrRollback() now drives the loop from the new side's own catalog rows alone (parent_table=events) and uses each row's range_start/range_end to bound a COUNT(*) query directly against events_legacy for that month (new helper countRowsInRange()). Also fixed tests/integration/par05_online_partition_conversion_test.zig's own local plat_partition_catalog fixture DDL, which was missing the created_at/updated_at columns the real 1148_par02_partition_catalog.sql migration defines and that the shared upsert helper requires -- this genuinely blocked verifying the fix live and was corrected inline as the minimal schema-parity fix, not deferred. Verified live against real PostgreSQL (BPM_TEST_DB_URL): test-integration-par05 is 6/6 pass (TC-PAR-05-06 specifically green, confirmed on two consecutive runs), up from 5/6 with "expected error.ConversionRowCountMismatch, found void" before this fix. zig build, zig build check (PI-03 gate: build + scoped zig fmt --check), and zig build test (1071/1135 pass, 64 skipped -- live-DB integration tests not run by this target, 0 failures) all exit 0. python tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests: 0 BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR. Confirmed no regression: test-integration-par06-reconstruction remains at its pre-existing 4/5 pass (TC-PAR-06-05, unrelated to partition_maintenance.zig/partition_conversion.zig, already reported at this same ratio in REWORK 2's own completion note, tracked under ISS-0678/GH-720, untouched here) and test-integration-pin01 remains at its pre-existing 8/9 pass + 1 crash (ISS-0680/GH-722's already-excluded resolve() leak, untouched here).
